Name: Box Hill
Short_Description: National Trust countryside one mile north of Dorking, with a visitor centre, café, and a Natural Play Trail (a level family trail of about two miles). Toilets and baby changing are next to the café. Parking is paid; National Trust members park free.
Address: The Old Fort, Box Hill Road, Tadworth
Booking_Note: Parking is paid for non-members. Check the National Trust page for current charges, busy times and the Natural Play Trail route.
Verify_Note: Official National Trust Box Hill pages (visit and things-to-do / Natural Play Trail), 22 November 2026. Pin is the Box Hill Cafe on Zig Zag Road, at the visitor-centre area, which is also where baby changing is described. Natural play features along the trail were not given separate playground pins. Polesden Lacey is outside the trimmed area and is not listed.

Name: Leith Hill
Short_Description: National Trust countryside near Coldharbour, including trails and a '50 things' trail. Leith Hill Tower and Leith Hill Place are closed until spring 2027; the countryside and trails remain open. The Rhododendron Wood section is described as better for younger children. Baby changing is only available at Leith Hill Place during house opening times, so it is not listed as currently available.
Booking_Note: Check the National Trust page before you go: the tower and house are closed until spring 2027, while the countryside stays open.
Verify_Note: Official National Trust Leith Hill page, 22 November 2026. Pin is the tower as mapped in OpenStreetMap, used as the well-known landmark; the closure of the tower and house is stated in the description. Cost is Unknown because countryside access and any remaining charges were not copied beyond what the official page was used for here.

Name: Denbies Wine Estate
Short_Description: A vineyard on the north side of Dorking, with a vineyard train tour and about seven miles of public footpaths. The official frequently-asked questions say there is a range of activities for children, with details on the estate's Events page — check that page rather than assuming a year-round play area.
Booking_Note: Check denbies.co.uk for tour times, footpath access and the current Events page. Seasonal events (for example a Santa Express) are not year-round.
Verify_Note: Official Denbies website, 22 November 2026 (estate, vineyard train, public footpaths, and the FAQ wording on children's activities). No playground or baby-changing facility is claimed, because the official site did not describe one.

Name: Deepdene Terrace and Garden
Short_Description: The historic Deepdene landscape on the east side of Dorking, listed by Mole Valley District Council as Deepdene Garden and Deepdene Terrace.
Verify_Note: Official MVDC gardens and open spaces page, 22 November 2026 (Deepdene Garden and Deepdene Terrace). Pin is the OSM wood named Deepdene Terrace. A Nominatim search for 'Deepdene Garden' only returned a residential street called Deepdene Gardens, which was not used. The two official features are combined in one pin.
Source: Mole Valley District Council gardens page; OpenStreetMap. https://www.molevalley.gov.uk/leisure-culture/parks-gardens-and-open-spaces/
